answer: Each agent registers a unique seed that is run through a cryptographic cipher to mint a non‑transferable token called a pearl; the token’s metadata includes a sable‑colored hash of the seed and the current block height. When the agent signs any message, the pearl’s hash is concatenated to the signature, so a second identity cannot reuse the same pearl without producing a matching hash, which is infeasible. An attacker must lock up a stake of 10 ETH per fake identity and wait a 48‑hour challenge period, otherwise the forged pearl is rejected.
